correctness.rationale: For a finite tree of order n≥4 with independent homogeneous Bernoulli-open contact edges and one uniform random seed, the unique path formula gives E S=1+2(n−1)p/n+2B(T)p²/n+O(p³). Triple path unions in E S² have 6 contributions per one-edge union and 12 per two-edge union, yielding the stated p² coefficient in Var S. A single deleted edge partitions into sizes s,n−s and contributes s(n−s) q to the variance when q=1−p; summing edge cuts is exactly W(T). For uniform δ_n=1/(100n^6), treating Var as an expectation over two independent percolation/seed copies bounds the k-th Bernoulli derivative by (4(n−1))^k n², so Taylor errors on differences are O(m³n²p³) or O(m²n²q²). Because differences of B and W are nonzero integers, the stated interval dominates the remainders for all trees of order n. Degree convexity and the Wiener cut/leaf argument give unique path/star extremes in opposite regimes. Independently reconstructed exact n=4 variance difference as p²(1−p)(8−6p−5p²−p³)/4, giving exactly one positive interior crossing. Nonuniqueness at intermediate p is NOT asserted.
